text:
marta: heads-up  found a weird one on the localized site: /zh/docs/guides/scale#autoscaling-behavior jumps to the wrong place (or not at all) after the docusaurus i18n build. nightly linkcheck flagged it. anyone seen locale fragment churn like this?

lee: yep, saw that in the nightly run. the English source has `### Autoscaling behavior {#autoscaling-behavior}` but the translated file lost the explicit id during the i18n extraction step, so the Chinese page generated a different slug like `autoscaling-behavior-2`.

sophie: sounds like the l10n tooling (crowdin / i18n extractor) is stripping `{#id}` annotations. I've seen that before when translators edit headings in the translation console. Two options: 1) enforce the id in the translated markdown as a translated note, or 2) add a short metadata id in the frontmatter we can keep consistent across locales.

link-bot: buildkite/docs-validate #1150 failed: missing fragment `/zh/docs/guides/scale#autoscaling-behavior` (3 occurrences)

marta: opened a WIP PR to add a frontmatter `canonical_id` and a small post-process step that rewrites translated markdown to include the explicit `{#...}` on headings based on that field. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4999

lee: interesting. example frontmatter patch in the PR: 
```yaml
---
title: 伸缩指南
canonical_id: autoscaling-behavior
---
```
then a tiny script inserts `{#autoscaling-behavior}` after the matching translated heading.

sophie: +1 on post-process. alternatively we could update the docusaurus i18n config to copy IDs from the source when generating translated site artifacts, but that's a deeper change and might not be supported by the extractor. Post-process is safer for now.

marta: added unit test to tools/linkcheck/tests that runs a localized build (`yarn build --locale zh`) and checks fragments across `build/zh`. snippet in the test: `assert grep -q 'id="autoscaling-behavior"' build/zh/docs/guides/scale/*.html`

ci-bot: buildkite/docs-validate #1152 started (locale-aware linkcheck)

lee: small gotcha: some headings in the translations were reworded and no longer match a simple regex. my script falls back to matching heading text by fuzzy compare and then injects the id. not perfect but covers 90% of cases. leaving a TODO to surface mismatches so translators can keep canonical ids.

sophie: we should add a line in the contributor guide & the translators' notes: "Do not remove or alter canonical header ids (canonical_id in frontmatter)." Saves future surprises.

link-bot: buildkite/docs-validate #1152 failed: 2 missing fragments remain in `build/zh` - `autoscaling-behavior` and `scale-examples`.

marta: reworked the script to fall back to searching by English-to-zh mapping table we have from the translation memory. pushed update to PR 4999. also added a small `tools/i18n/verify_ids.py` that scans `i18n/zh/d/**` and reports headings without a canonical id.

lee: re-ran local `yarn build:docs --locale=zh` and `./tools/linkcheck/check_fragments.sh build/zh`. both pass now.

ci-bot: buildkite/docs-validate #1156 succeeded: locale linkcheck passed, no missing fragments.

marta: merged PR 4999 at 1800000048. left a release-note entry: "docs(i18n): preserve canonical header ids across translations to stabilize fragment links; add locale-aware linkcheck and post-process step."

sophie: follow-up: adding a short paragraph under "Writing docs" and under "Translators" explaining canonical_id/frontmatter practice and an example. i'll open PR for the styleguide blurb.

lee: and i'll add a CI job to run linkcheck for `en, zh, ja` on every docs PR so we catch regressions early.

marta: perfect. thanks all  closing the loop.
